coach.pitch: A 15-year-old national-level youth player who was recently where your child is now — and can explain exactly how to make the next jump.
audience: Club players up to ~1600 rating who want to climb
Kids and teens preparing for their first rated tournaments
format: 1-on-1 lessons online via Lichess or Chess.com analysis boards
Video call on Zoom or Google Meet
Personal game analysis after every lesson
Homework puzzles and a training plan between lessons

method.name: Openings that grow with you
method.detail: Learn the system Aakrit used to climb from 1543 to 2000+: the Accelerated London as White and the Sicilian Dragon as Black — sound, easy to learn, hard to refute.

method.name: Tactics that stick
method.detail: Structured puzzle training matched to your level, with patterns to recognise for a lifetime.

method.name: Your own games as the textbook
method.detail: Every lesson is built around your games: what happened, why, and the one habit to fix next.

method.name: Tournament preparation
method.detail: Time management, clock technique and nerves — learned from 8 years and 75+ rated tournaments in three countries.

faq.a: From complete beginners (learning the moves) up to players around 1600. If you're above that, Aakrit will tell you honestly and can help you find the right trainer.
Mostly kids and teens (6–16), because Aakrit is 15 and pupils relate to a coach close to their age. Adult beginners are also welcome.

faq.q: Which language are the lessons in?
faq.a: English, German or Hindi — whichever your child is most comfortable in. Growing up in Berlin and the Netherlands and playing in India, Aakrit speaks all three fluently.
You get a video call link (Zoom or Google Meet) and a shared analysis board on Lichess or Chess.com. All your child needs is a laptop or tablet — no chess set required.

faq.q: Is the trial lesson really free?
faq.a: Yes — 20 minutes, no commitment, no payment details. It's the easiest way to see if the coaching is a good fit.

faq.q: How do I book and pay?
faq.a: Pick a time via the booking link on this page. Payment is by Tikkie (Netherlands), bank transfer or PayPal — details are confirmed when you book.

faq.q: What time zones do you teach in?
faq.a: Aakrit is based in the Netherlands (CET/CEST), so evening slots work well for Europe; weekend mornings also work for families in India.
Not yet — 1-on-1 gives the fastest improvement. Small groups (2–4 kids) may be added later; ask via the contact section.
